full_judgment:
40. In Mussauddin Ahmed vs State of Assam, (2009) 14 SCC 541, is a case for drawing an adverse presumption for withholding vital witnesses. The case is one of rape and the court noticed that the victim claimed her age as thirteen years, the medical evidence shows that she was eighteen years and that it was an unnatural death. None of the family members of the prosecutrix came to the scene. Her parents or either of them or any other family members could be most reliable or natural witness on the point of her age. The court drew adverse inference against the prosecution story. This case does not help to the accused persons. 

 IV. For that the High Court Division has failed to consider that the most important FIR named witnesses, i.e. Driver Mokbul Hossain and Abdul Halim and important disinterested reliable neighbor of the alleged place of occurrence and some of the important witnesses those who were cited in the charge sheet have been withheld from the prosecution without any reasonings whatsoever, which is fatal for the prosecution and deserves presumption in as much as the conviction and sentence is based upon the testimony of interested, dubious and unworthy chance witnesses and thus the conviction and sentence is not maintainable in law and liable to be set aside." 

 122. Besides driver-Md Moquebul Hossain and relative-Md Halim, the parents of the deceased and the other family members of the deceased also appear to me very natural, important and vital witnesses to depose as to the fact of calling for the deceased by Biddut. This will be clear if look at the other evidence of PWs 1 and 11. PW1 admitted in his cross-examination that his parents were alive, they were five brothers including the deceased and four sisters and they lived together along with parents. He further admitted that during investigation, the Investigation Officer examined his elder brother, AK Azad, his wife and other members of his family. The PW admitted that except himself, none of his family members has been cited as a witness in the case. PW11 also stated in his cross-examination that the deceased was bachelor and his main guardian was his father. If the version of PW 1 that accused-Biddut called for the deceased on 27-1-1997 after 4-30 pm to have Iftar and then he did not return in the night was true, it was natural that he (PW 1) would disclose the said fact to the other family members of his family, particularly, the parents and in that case, they all would have looked for the deceased. It is also more interesting that as per the testimony of PW 1, he only looked for the deceased and telephoned at different places when the deceased allegedly did not return home in the night. When the parents were alive and their son did not return home in the night, they would have been very much anxious to look for their son, but they did not, this is unusual and speaks a volume. PW 11 also admitted that the parents of the deceased were examined, but their statements were not recorded. My common sense failed to visualize any reason when the parents were examined by PW 11, why their statements were not recorded and for what reason and on what logic, they were not cited in the charge sheet as witnesses and examined in the case as witnesses and this facts also clearly gives rise to an adverse presumption against the prosecution within the meaning of illustration (g) of section 114 of the Evidence Act that had the parents and other members of the family been examined, they would not have supported the prosecution case. And, in fact, suggestion to that effect was given to both PW 1 and PW 11. 

 124. From the judgment of the High Court Division, it appears that it took very lightly the adverse presumption that arose against the prosecution for non-citing and non-examining driver-Moquebul Hossain and Md Halim in view of the provision of section 114(g) of the Evidence Act as it observed: 

 149. The testimonies of PW 8 cannot be believed to be true, admittedly he was examined by the last Investigation Officer, PW 11 on 22-12-1997, i.e. after 11 (eleven) months of the date of occurrence (occurrence took place on 27-1-1997) and 9 (nine) months of his taking charge of the investigation of the case (PW 11 took up the investigation of the case on 15-3-1997). The reason is no explanation whatsoever has been given either by the PW or by PW 11 for such belated examination and disclosure of facts. It is to be further noted that as per own admission of PW 8, he ran his pan shop from the early part of January, 1996 till August, 1997, i.e. after the alleged occurrence, he allegedly ran his shop for 7(seven) long months and during this period of long 7(seven) months, he did not tell anybody about the fact that he saw the accused taking a person and then throwing him by the side of the rail line. This PW in cross-examination has further stated that during this period, neither any uniformed Police nor any civil dressed Police either examined him or interrogated him. Another very significant fact is that this PW stated in his cross-examination that he stated the fact of seeing the occurrence of throwing the dead body by the accused to Dulal a boy of Jahad Hotel after 1/1½ month of the occurrence and Dulal though cited as a witness was also not examined by the prosecution. And no explanation whatsoever was given by the prosecution for his non-examination; this also creates an adverse presumption against the prosecution case as to the last link of the chain of circumstances in view of illustration (g) of section 114 of the Evidence Act. But unfortunately, the High Court Division without giving the benefit of said adverse presumption to the accused argued on behalf of the prosecution and gave an explanation by observing that "It transpires from the LCR that hotel boy Dulal was also examined by investigating officer under section 161 of the Code on 18-10-1997 and he is a cited witness, but he did not come to depose in the Court. It is, however, not expected that such a poor employee of Jahad Hotel would come to give testimony against his master's full brother (accused Karzon)." The fact that PW 8 did not tell the fact of seeing the accused taking a person holding and then throwing him by the side of rail line for such a long time coupled with absurdity and improbability in his story that though he passed matriculation in 1963, came to Dhaka for a job in January, 1995 though he had 5 (five) bighas land and one of his sons is a business man in Chittagong and the evidence of PW 11 that there was no proof that he (PW 8) used to run a pan shop in front of Jahad Hotel at Mohakhali totally make the testimonies of PW 8 unbelievable, but unfortunately, the High Court Division did not at all consider the apparent prima facie factual aspect of the case and the legal presumption against the prosecution that steamed in view of the provisions of illustration (g) of section 114 of the Evidence Act.
